clue.text: Bus pranged in pound is okay

indicators.note: a pranged vehicle has been crashed and bent out of shape, so its letters are knocked into a new order
one set of letters is placed inside another, as something sits in a pen

blocks.note: to pound is to thump, hit hard
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A bus has crashed into the car pound, and someone shrugs that it's fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The crumpled bus goes between the last two letters of a word for pound, giving THUMBS UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumbs up is the gesture of approval, so giving the thumbs up is giving your okay.

clue.text: Encourage judge in that case to release husband

indicators.note: releasing someone lets them go, so a letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a judge hears a case in court
then, as in 'if so, then'
H for husband, the letter that leaves

explanation.surface: A plea urging a judge in a divorce case to free a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: THEN lets go of its H to become TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to give them heart, to cheer and embolden them, which is encouraging them.

clue.text: Titled woman makes Roman Catholic greeting unique through church service

indicators.note: one set of letters runs through the middle of another, splitting it

blocks.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
hi is a greeting
one, as in one of a kind
Mass is the Catholic church service

explanation.surface: A noblewoman gives a unique Catholic welcome during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unique' is not an adjective describing the greeting; it stands for the number of a thing that is one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a woman holding the rank of marquess, or a marquess's wife, a noble title.

clue.text: Power seized by visionary wartime architect

indicators.note: something seized is grabbed and held, so it ends up inside the grabber

blocks.note: a seer is a visionary, one who sees the future
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A visionary wartime architect grabs power.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Speer was Hitler's architect and later his armaments minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Speer designed buildings for the Nazi regime and ran its war production, an architect of the Second World War era.

clue.text: Sportsman with second eleven to swap places next month

indicators.note: the two pieces that follow the sportsman trade positions, so they are joined in the opposite order to the clue

blocks.note: a pro is a professional sportsman
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a team of eleven
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A sportsman in the second eleven is set to change positions next month.
explanation.walkthrough: Old business-letter style: 'proximo' means of next month, as 'ultimo' means of last month.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximo is a Latin-derived term in formal correspondence for the following month.

clue.text: Siberian father offends at first Buddhist school

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word it follows, offends

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the first letter of offends
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A Siberian priest gives offence to a Buddhist school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siberian' looks like it describes the father, but it is the definition, used as an adjective for icy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberian is used loosely for bitterly cold conditions, like those of Siberia, so it works as an adjective for frozen.

clue.text: Surveyor reserving a seat for the bishop to eat this?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: a dish someone might eat

indicators.note: reserving means keeping something back, so one word holds a letter within it

blocks.note: FRICS stands for Fellow of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors
taken as written
a see is a bishop's seat, his diocese

explanation.surface: A surveyor saving a chair for the bishop so he can sit down to his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A chartered surveyor puts letters after their name for the professional body; 'for the bishop' says which kind of seat is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a stew of sliced meat in a white sauce, something one might eat.

clue.text: Rotten to put disc on very loudly

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece put on another sits above it

blocks.note: O is round, like a disc
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone complains it's rotten to put a record on at full blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is rotten; off means spoiled or bad.

clue.text: Firm guarantee

blocks.note: first meaning: resolute, serious in intent
second meaning: a token payment given as a pledge that a bargain will be kept

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a company's warranty; 'Firm' is an adjective, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and determined, and an earnest is also a deposit pledging that a deal will be honoured.

clue.text: Go with free trade — if prepared to see consensus is impossible

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked up from raw material, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trade negotiators accept free trade on condition, but realise they will never fully agree.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is split by the link word 'with': GO plus FREE TRADE IF, thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree to differ is to accept that a dispute will not be settled, recognising that consensus cannot be reached.

clue.text: Artist such as Rembrandt cold in the upper air

indicators.note: one item is placed inside another, the cold put in the air

blocks.note: the ether is an old poetic word for the upper regions of the air
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A Dutch master painter shivers high up in the chilly atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt made many fine etchings as well as paintings, so he is an example of a printmaker who works on etched plates.

clue.text: I am no spring chicken, having to stay at home in thought

indicators.note: having means holding or keeping, so one group of letters keeps another inside it

blocks.note: I am contracts to I'm
no spring chicken is an idiom for no longer young
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: An elderly person explains they'd rather stay home and be lost in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thought' looks like a noun completing 'in thought', but it is a past-tense verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagined and thought are both past tenses meaning conceived or supposed in the mind.

clue.text: Lawmaker one spots in town as dishevelled

indicators.note: dishevelled means messed up and untidy, so these letters are put in disorder

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
acne is an outbreak of spots
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scruffy politician with a spotty face is seen around town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawmaker' suggests a legislator, but these are laws of physics, not parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton formulated the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, a maker of scientific laws.

clue.text: As War and Peace to corporal an old American holds captive

definitions.note: a comparison phrase: describing a pair like war and peace

indicators.note: a captor holds someone inside, so the outer letters keep the others enclosed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Corporal Nym is a soldier in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor
O is a standard abbreviation for old
US for American

explanation.surface: A corporal who has read Tolstoy's War and Peace is taken prisoner by an elderly American.
explanation.walkthrough: AN, O and US together hold TO and NYM. 'War and Peace' looks like the novel, but here it is just two opposite words.
explanation.definitionFit: War and peace are opposites, words with contrary meanings, so a pair like them is antonymous.

clue.text: Song about break-up from dearest, reeling in the years

indicators.note: a break-up smashes a word apart so its letters can come back in another order
reeling in is pulling a catch inside, so the outer letters draw the rest in between them

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, so two of them for years
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A song about splitting from a loved one and looking back on the years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the title of Steely Dan's 'Reelin' in the Years'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday is the Beatles song by Paul McCartney about a lost love, one of the most covered songs ever.

clue.text: Does spiritual work

blocks.note: first meaning: performs, carries out
second meaning: the book of the New Testament recounting the apostles' deeds

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone doing charitable or religious work; 'Does' is a plain verb and the rest names a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means performs or behaves, and the New Testament book telling of the early church carries the same name.

clue.text: Clever start to a Napoleonic palindrome?

blocks.note: first meaning: skilful, capable
second meaning: the opening word of the palindrome credited to Napoleon on his exile to Elba

explanation.walkthrough: The palindrome is 'Able was I ere I saw Elba', supposedly said by Napoleon; the question mark flags the playful second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled or competent, and it is also the first word of the famous Elba palindrome.

clue.text: Snake covers half the territory

indicators.note: to cover something is to go round it, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a boa is a constricting snake
hemi- is the prefix meaning half, as in hemisphere

explanation.surface: A snake spreads itself over half the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the territory' tempts you to take half the letters of territory; half is HEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia is a historical kingdom and region, now the western part of the Czech Republic, a territory in central Europe.

clue.text: One shelled on beach needs rest by river in Hackney

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside a word, as a passenger sits in a vehicle

blocks.note: in snooker a spider is a raised rest for the cue
a hackney carriage is the formal name for a London taxi
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tired creature on the shore needs a lie-down beside the river in Hackney, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hackney' looks like the London borough, but it is a cab. The snooker spider is a cue rest with a high arched head.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider crab is a long-legged crab with a hard carapace, a shelled creature often found on the shore.

clue.text: An old European, NKVD leader, wearing clothes

indicators.note: used as a verb, clothes means dresses, wrapping one word around the other

blocks.note: someone wearing a coat is in it
Lavrentiy Beria headed the NKVD, Stalin's secret police

explanation.surface: An old European, once head of the Soviet secret police, is described in his outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'NKVD leader' wants to give the letter N; it is the man who led it. 'clothes' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberians were an ancient people of Spain and Portugal, so an Iberian is an early European.

clue.text: Social workers are brought in, making brilliant point

indicators.note: bringing something in puts it inside, so a word goes within the other

blocks.note: ants are social insects, and the workers of their colony
taken as written

explanation.surface: Social workers are called in and make a clever argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social workers' suggests the profession; here it is insects. A point is a point of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is a red supergiant in Scorpius, one of the brightest stars, seen as a shining point in the night sky.

clue.text: Gas pressure gone — she worried

indicators.note: to be worried is to be agitated and churned up, so these letters are shaken into another order

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman frets that the gas pressure has dropped to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosgene is a poisonous gas, used as a chemical weapon in the First World War.

clue.text: Energy-saving old car found

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe, so one set of letters holds another within it

blocks.note: a crate is slang for an old, rickety car
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An economical old car has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy-saving' looks like one adjective, but the hyphen hides a symbol plus a container signal. 'found' is a verb, not the past of find.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something, such as a school or company, is to establish it, to create it from nothing.

clue.text: Punch a companion

blocks.note: to chin someone is British slang for punching them on the jaw
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hit a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang, a china is a mate or close friend, so it serves for a companion.

clue.text: Run without care from clergyman passing mother and boy

indicators.note: the clergyman comes after the others, as if he has walked by them and now stands behind

blocks.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
a lad is a boy
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A careless runner gets away from a priest walking past a mother and her son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is not about sprinting; it means manage, as in running a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To maladminister is to manage affairs badly, which is running them carelessly.

clue.text: Blue jay appearing regularly comes to meadow

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every second letter shows

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A blue jay lands regularly in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic word for a grassy field or pasture, a meadow.

clue.text: Homosexual admits showing scant regard for morals in mutually attracted group

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word lets another inside it

blocks.note: gay is a synonym
lax means loose in conduct or standards

explanation.surface: A gay man confesses to loose morals within a group of people drawn to one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like a circle of lovers; it is the gravity that binds stars together.
explanation.definitionFit: A galaxy is a vast system of stars held together by their mutual gravitational attraction.

clue.text: Straight to headland for simple elegance

blocks.note: neat means undiluted, as a straight drink is
a ness is a headland, common in British place names

explanation.surface: Heading straight to the headland gives a simple, elegant walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness is tidiness and trim simplicity, a plain kind of elegance.
